Tl; dr: Bernie Sanders is not a Democrat, he is an independent. Ergo, the Democratic Party was not under any obligation to show him any fairness during the primary elections.

Bernie Sanders was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1991. He was then elected to the US Senate in 2007. During this whole time, he has represented the State of Vermont as an Independent. Since 1991, "he has caucused with the Democratic Party, which has entitled him to committee assignments and at times given Democrats a majority."

However, the most recent election "was the only time in Sanders' career that he publicly identified as a Democrat, and he has since announced he will return to the Senate as an independent."

Sanders clearly leans left and his values overlap Democrat positions much more than Republicans. But he has achieved a large part of his notoriety by being an independent. It’s doubtful he would have been as well known if he was a registered Democrat. Political parties are groups with an identity and he has willingly chosen not to identify as Democrat all these years, for good and bad.

To put this in perspective, the other Senator from Vermont is Patrick Leahy, also a Democrat. Leahy was elected to the United States Senate for the first time in November 1974 and is currently the longest-serving Democratic Senator. Although Leahy has had a long and distinguished career, he probably was not as well known to Bernie Bros prior to the most recent election. Part of this is that Leahy has served as a Democrat all these years while Sanders has chosen to remain an independent.

Disclaimer 1: This doesn’t mean the DNC should dismiss someone who generates a lot of enthusiasm, just that they were under no obligation to treat him fairly.

Disclaimer 2: A lot of this criticism is similar to the situation between Donald Trump and the RNC.
